term: I am: speech form, contextual interpretation and actual divine authority
resolution: The John statements are textual attributions and narrated actions; the signature divine-authority predicate concerns an actual claim and is not defined by an occurrence of I am. Ordinary self-identification at 9.9 and the before-Abraham contrast at 8.58 are contextually distinct uses. Personal preexistence, divine-name echo, ideal priority in God’s purpose, delegated agency and divine identity are not synonyms. The note docs/john-abraham-saying.md preserves their positive accounts and different obligations. Neither an ordinary-use control nor hostile stones settles the contextual reading of 8.58. No equation with the Creed, God predicate, historical utterance or actual divine authority is supplied.
